name: Bal Mithai
instructions: 1. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan and add khoya, roasting it on low heat until it turns a deep brown color.
2. Add sugar to the roasted khoya and stir continuously until the mixture thickens and begins to leave the sides of the pan.
3. Pour the mixture into a greased tray and spread it evenly to a thickness of about an inch.
4. While the mixture is still slightly warm, cut it into square or rectangular cubes.
5. Press the white sugar balls firmly onto the surface of each piece.
6. Allow the mithai to cool completely and set before serving.
description: Bal Mithai is a quintessential sweet from the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand, particularly famous in Almora. It is a brown, chocolate-colored fudge made from khoya, coated in crunchy white sugar balls. Historically, it was an offering to local deities and remains a beloved cultural symbol of the Himalayan mountain state.
